niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right one depends on your goals, budget, industry, geographies and whether you need brand-awareness, direct-response, or measurement-first work. Below I’ll give a short framework to pick the right partner, a list of reputable agency/platform options by type, the key questions to ask, and the metrics you should expect.

Quick guidance
- If you need broad reach, premium inventory and full-service planning: consider a large media agency with strong CTV capabilities (WPP/GroupM, Omnicom, Publicis, IPG, Dentsu).
- If you want programmatic, audience-targeting and performance optimization: look at DSP-led or specialist shops (The Trade Desk + performance-focused agencies; programmatic CTV specialists).
- If you want platform-native work (Roku, Samsung TV, Hulu, Amazon Fire TV): either work directly with the platform’s advertising group or an agency that has official partnerships and creative experience for those platforms.
- If you’re a smaller/fast-moving brand: boutique or performance agencies with proven CTV case studies (independent media/commerce agencies) often move faster and cost less.

Examples of reputable partners (by type)
- Global/full-service media groups: GroupM (Wavemaker, Mindshare), Omnicom (OMD, PHD), Publicis (Starcom, Spark Foundry), IPG (UM, Initiative), Dentsu (Carat, iProspect).
- Programmatic/activation platforms (often used by agencies): The Trade Desk, Google DV360, Amazon DSP, Roku OneView.
- Platform-native ad teams: Roku Advertising, Samsung Ads, Hulu/Disney advertising sales, Amazon Ads (Fire TV).
- Measurement/CTV specialists and creative-adtech: VideoAmp (measurement + activation), Innovid (creative & ad serving), Tremor Video, Magnite (SSP).
- Boutiques and performance agencies (examples—good for mid-market to direct-response): Tinuiti, Horizon Media, independents with CTV case studies (choose one with relevant vertical experience).

How to choose — evaluation checklist
- Campaign goal fit: brand lift vs direct response vs online conversions vs in-store visits.
- Inventory access: premium publishers, app/streaming partners, platform partnerships (Roku, Samsung, Hulu, vMVPDs).
- Buying approach: direct-sold vs programmatic vs PMP; ability to do guaranteed/flexible buys.
- Targeting capabilities: household, demographic, interest, or cross-device/identity solutions.
- Measurement: third-party verification, viewability, brand-lift studies, incrementality testing, attribution to sales.
- Creative capabilities: 16:9 vs 4:3 cuts, interactive overlays, dynamic creative optimization for CTV.
- Fraud/malvertising protection and transparency on fees / media buys.
- Reporting cadence and dashboards; access to raw data.
- References and case studies in your vertical and for your goals.

Key questions to ask any agency
- Can you show campaign case studies with measurable outcomes for CTV?
- How do you buy inventory (platforms, private marketplaces, direct deals)?
- What targeting signals and identity partners do you use?
- How will you measure ROI and prove incrementality?
- What creative formats do you recommend and can you produce them?
- What are your fees and how transparent are media costs?
- Who will own the data and reporting?

Typical KPIs to expect
- Reach, frequency, and unique households reached
- View-through rate / completion rate (for video)
- Brand lift (ad recall, awareness, consideration)
- Cost metrics: CPM, cost-per-completed-view
- Downstream metrics if performance-focused: site visits, conversions, ROAS, foot traffic lift
- Incrementality (A/B or holdout test results)

If you want, tell me:
- campaign goal (awareness vs performance),
- monthly budget,
- geography (US, global, specific countries),
- industry (retail, DTC, finance, CPG, etc.),
and I’ll recommend 3–5 agencies or platform partners that would be the best fit and explain why.
